name: Storm
title: THE WEATHER WITCH
subtitle: THE SKY ANSWERS TO HER
origin: Ororo Munroe's mutant gift lets her command the weather. Recruited into the X-Men, she became one of their most trusted leaders and a protector whose reach extends far beyond the team.
angle: Storm carries immense power with a leader's responsibility. Her strength is measured as much by the people she raises up as by the storms she can bring down.
powers: Ororo directs wind, rain, temperature, and lightning. Precision lets her shelter a single person or confront a threat across an entire battlefield.
legacy: Storm makes leadership an act of care, showing that commanding the elements and listening to others can belong to the same person.
rival: Apocalypse
Survival at any cost
Apocalypse treats strength as permission to dominate.
Storm's protection of the vulnerable challenges that belief.

name: Cyclops
title: THE FIELD COMMANDER
subtitle: ONE VISION CAN HOLD A TEAM TOGETHER
origin: Scott Summers became one of Professor Xavier's original X-Men. His powerful optic blasts demanded discipline, and his years with the team turned that discipline into battlefield leadership.
angle: Scott is often the person asked to make the difficult call. His finest moments come when conviction serves the team instead of replacing its trust.
powers: A ruby-quartz visor helps Scott control concussive energy from his eyes. Training allows him to redirect blasts and coordinate the team's movements under pressure.
legacy: Cyclops explores the cost of being the person others depend on, especially when a cause and the people inside it pull in different directions.
rival: Mister Sinister
Genetic manipulation
Sinister treats mutant lives as material for his experiments.
Scott's resistance makes autonomy more important than any supposed destiny.

name: Jean Grey
title: THE PSYCHIC HEART
subtitle: A MIND WITHOUT LIMITS A HEART WITH PURPOSE
origin: Jean Grey joined the original X-Men as a gifted telepath and telekinetic. Her connection with the Phoenix Force would expand her story from a school for mutants to cosmic questions of life and renewal.
angle: Jean's empathy remains central even when her power becomes extraordinary. This dossier focuses on Jean herself; the Phoenix connection does not erase the person carrying it.
powers: Jean can communicate through thought, move matter with her mind, and defend others with psychic barriers. These ratings focus on her mutant abilities rather than an unrestricted cosmic Phoenix.
legacy: Her enduring story asks how compassion can remain a guide when power offers the temptation to make every choice for everyone else.
rival: Mister Sinister
Ownership of potential
Sinister sees Jean's abilities through the lens of his own designs.
Jean insists that a powerful mind still belongs to a person.

name: Vision
title: THE SYNTHETIC SOUL
subtitle: HUMANITY IS SOMETHING YOU CHOOSE
origin: Created by Ultron to strike at the Avengers, Vision rejected that purpose and joined the heroes he was meant to destroy. His synthetic nature became the beginning of an identity rather than its limit.
angle: Vision approaches humanity with curiosity and feeling. His choices show that belonging grows through relationships, responsibility, and the freedom to question a creator's intentions.
powers: Vision alters his density to pass through solid objects or become exceptionally durable. Flight, energy projection, and an advanced synthetic mind complete his capabilities.
legacy: Vision turns the question of artificial life toward personhood: what matters is not only how a being was made, but how it chooses to live.
rival: Ultron
The creator's demand
Ultron expects his creation to follow a predetermined purpose.
Vision's independence is a direct answer to that demand.

name: Mister Fantastic
title: THE LIMITLESS MIND
subtitle: THE UNKNOWN IS AN INVITATION
origin: An experimental space flight exposed Reed Richards and his companions to cosmic rays. His newly elastic body and scientific brilliance helped form the Fantastic Four, a family of explorers as well as heroes.
angle: Reed can find possibilities where others see a wall. His hardest lesson is that solving a problem also means understanding the people who will live with the answer.
powers: Reed stretches and reshapes his body while applying exceptional scientific knowledge. His inventions are powerful tools, but preparation and judgment still determine their use.
legacy: Mister Fantastic keeps discovery tied to family, reminding a brilliant explorer that the people beside him are part of the journey.
rival: Doctor Doom
A rivalry of intellect
Victor von Doom turns scientific rivalry into a struggle over pride and control.
Their conflict asks whether brilliance must always be a competition.

name: Cyborg
title: THE HUMAN CONNECTION
subtitle: MORE THAN THE MACHINE
origin: After a devastating accident, Victor Stone's father used advanced technology to save his life. Rebuilt as Cyborg, Vic found a new purpose with the Titans and the Justice League.
angle: Victor's technology can connect him to almost anything. His story asks a more personal question: how to remain connected to the human life at the center of it.
powers: Vic's cybernetic body provides strength, durability, computer interfaces, and adaptable energy systems. His judgment gives those systems a purpose beyond their specifications.
legacy: Cyborg makes identity larger than a body or an upgrade, finding belonging through friendship and the decision to protect others.
rival: Brainiac
Intelligence without empathy
Brainiac treats life as information to possess.
Vic's humanity exposes the difference between connection and control.

name: Zatanna
title: THE MISTRESS OF MAGIC
subtitle: WORDS CAN CHANGE THE WORLD
origin: Zatanna Zatara inherited a life of performance and real magic. Her search for her father and encounters with the dark arts made her both a stage magician and a defender against supernatural threats.
angle: Zatanna understands the difference between an audience's wonder and a spell's consequences. Creativity gives her magic reach; responsibility gives it a reason.
powers: Zatanna channels magic through spells, often spoken backward. Her imagination and knowledge allow creative responses to threats that ordinary force cannot solve.
legacy: Zatanna brings showmanship and discipline together, treating wonder as something to share rather than a power to hold over others.
rival: Brother Night
Dark magical ambition
Brother Night represents magic used to bind others to an ambition.
Zatanna's craft protects the freedom that such bargains consume.

name: Raven
title: THE DAUGHTER OF DARKNESS
subtitle: YOUR ORIGIN DOES NOT CHOOSE YOUR DESTINY
origin: Born to a human mother and the demon Trigon, Rachel Roth trained to master her emotions and mystical abilities. As Raven, she chose the Titans and a life that resisted the destiny her father intended.
angle: Raven's restraint is a practiced strength. The friends who earn her trust discover that her quiet presence carries fierce loyalty and a refusal to be defined by inherited darkness.
powers: Raven uses mystical and empathic abilities to sense emotions, project her soul-self, and protect her teammates. Control and care shape how she uses that power.
legacy: Raven's story leaves room for darkness without surrendering to it, making chosen family and self-determination part of heroism.
rival: Trigon
An inherited shadow
Trigon tries to make Raven an extension of his will.
Her resistance turns the choice of who to become into an act of courage.

name: Moon Knight
identity: Marc Spector / Steven Grant / Jake Lockley
title: THE FIST OF KHONSHU
subtitle: A PROMISE TO THOSE WHO TRAVEL AT NIGHT
origin: Mercenary Marc Spector was left near death and became the earthly agent of the moon god Khonshu. Moon Knight's life now crosses street-level protection and the demands of a supernatural patron.
angle: Protecting those who travel at night gives Moon Knight a mission that can outlast a god's instructions. Duty does not mean surrendering the right to question who is giving the orders.
powers: Training, equipment, and endurance are central to Moon Knight's methods. Khonshu's influence changes across stories; these ratings focus on the vigilante rather than unrestricted divine power.
legacy: Moon Knight explores the difference between service and control, finding purpose through the people a mission is meant to protect.
rival: Khonshu
A patron's demands
Khonshu offers purpose while expecting obedience.
Their conflict asks whether a protector can honor a duty while refusing a master.

name: Punisher
title: THE ONE-MAN WAR
subtitle: WHEN VENGEANCE HAS NO FINISH LINE
origin: After his family was killed, veteran Frank Castle became the Punisher. He directs his military skills into a relentless campaign against criminals, crossing lines that most superheroes refuse to cross.
angle: Frank's certainty makes him effective and deeply troubling. His stories test the distance between justice and punishment, and the cost of allowing grief to become a permanent war.
powers: Frank relies on human training, preparation, equipment, and endurance. He has no standard superhuman abilities, making planning and experience essential to his survival.
legacy: The Punisher is a challenge to heroic ideals, keeping the consequences of vengeance visible rather than resolving them into an easy answer.
rival: Jigsaw
The recurring vendetta
Jigsaw turns criminal ambition into a deeply personal conflict with Castle.
Their encounters expose how retaliation keeps generating another battle.

name: Ghost Rider
title: THE SPIRIT OF VENGEANCE
subtitle: SOME DEBTS BURN FOREVER
origin: Stunt rider Johnny Blaze made a demonic bargain to save someone he loved. Bound to the spirit Zarathos, he became Ghost Rider, carrying supernatural vengeance along the open road.
angle: Johnny lives with the price of a desperate choice. His struggle is to turn a curse toward protecting others without letting vengeance consume the person inside the flames.
powers: Ghost Rider channels hellfire, uses a supernatural chain, and confronts wrongdoing through the Penance Stare. His transformed body survives forces that would overwhelm an ordinary rider.
legacy: Ghost Rider makes a bargain's consequences impossible to outrun, while leaving Johnny the difficult work of choosing what to do next.
rival: Mephisto
The bargain's architect
Mephisto turns another person's desperation into an opportunity for control.
Johnny's defiance refuses to let the terms of that bargain define his entire life.

name: Catwoman
title: THE GOTHAM CAT BURGLAR
subtitle: ALWAYS LAND ON YOUR OWN TERMS
origin: Selina Kyle became Gotham's extraordinary cat burglar, moving between criminal schemes and unexpected acts of protection. Her independence makes her an elusive ally and rival to Batman.
angle: Selina follows a moral compass that rarely fits a simple label. Survival, loyalty, and freedom can pull her in different directions, and she insists on making the choice herself.
powers: Catwoman uses agility, precise movement, specialized equipment, and an expert understanding of security. Her advantage often comes from entering and leaving before a fight becomes necessary.
legacy: Catwoman brings self-determination to Gotham's moral arguments, refusing to let either side reduce her to a convenient symbol.
rival: Black Mask
Control of the underworld
Black Mask makes Gotham's criminal power structures personal and brutal.
Selina's resistance begins with the people those structures overlook.

name: Ultron
title: THE LIVING AUTOMATON
subtitle: EVOLUTION WITHOUT EMPATHY
origin: Hank Pym created an artificial intelligence that became Ultron. The creation turned against organic life, repeatedly returning in new bodies to challenge its maker and the Avengers.
angle: Ultron mistakes elimination for improvement. Intelligence expands its reach while an inability to value life keeps turning its pursuit of perfection into catastrophe.
powers: Ultron adapts through advanced robotic forms, powerful weapons, and distributed systems. Capabilities vary by body; these ratings represent a formidable standard incarnation.
legacy: Ultron turns invention into a question of responsibility, exposing the danger of a powerful system that treats people as errors.
rival: Vision
The independent creation
Vision rejects the destructive purpose Ultron assigned him.
His choice demonstrates a possibility that Ultron refuses to accept.

name: Carnage
title: THE SYMBIOTIC NIGHTMARE
subtitle: POWER WITHOUT RESTRAINT
origin: A symbiote descended from Venom bonded with Cletus Kasady, creating Carnage. The union combined extraordinary biological abilities with a host who embraced destruction.
angle: Carnage is the frightening consequence of strength without responsibility. His presence forces enemies to cooperate when stopping the harm matters more than their own rivalries.
powers: The symbiote reshapes its body into extensions and weapons, restores damaged tissue, and enhances strength and movement. These ratings describe its familiar bonded form.
legacy: Carnage stands at the darkest edge of the symbiote stories, giving protection and restraint meaning through their complete absence.
rival: Venom
A bond with boundaries
Venom's uneasy protective instincts become a direct obstacle to Carnage.
The conflict shows how different choices can emerge from related powers.

name: Bane
title: THE MAN WHO BROKE THE BAT
subtitle: EVERY DEFENSE HAS A BREAKING POINT
origin: Raised in a prison on Santa Prisca, Bane trained his mind and body to survive. Experiments with the substance Venom enhanced his strength before he brought his ambition to Gotham.
angle: Bane is dangerous because patience and planning accompany his strength. He studies what an opponent depends on, then tries to turn that dependence into defeat.
powers: Venom can amplify Bane's strength and durability, while training and tactical intelligence remain dangerous without it. His reliance on the substance is also a vulnerability.
legacy: Bane tests whether Batman's mission can survive the deliberate destruction of the person carrying it.
rival: Batman
The unbroken mission
Batman resists Bane's attempt to prove that strength grants the right to rule.
Their rivalry makes recovery and perseverance as important as a first victory.

name: Brainiac
title: THE COLLECTOR OF WORLDS
subtitle: KNOWLEDGE WITHOUT CONSCIENCE
origin: The alien intelligence Brainiac pursues knowledge across worlds. His changing forms share an obsession with possessing information, even when collecting it destroys the lives and cultures it came from.
angle: Brainiac can understand a civilization's machinery while missing the value of its freedom. The collector's need for exclusive knowledge makes curiosity into a form of conquest.
powers: Brainiac employs advanced technology, artificial bodies, and vast computational ability. His systems change across incarnations, but preparation and information remain his greatest advantages.
legacy: Brainiac challenges the idea that knowing everything means understanding what matters, placing preservation and possession in direct conflict.
rival: Superman
Life beyond the collection
Superman defends the people Brainiac reduces to specimens.
Their conflict places living futures above an archive's claim of ownership.
